topic.name: Moments of Inertia of Laminas About the Coordinate Axes

question.text: A rectangular plate of mass $M\,\textrm{kg}$ and uniform mass density occupies the region $ D = \big\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq y \leq 2 \big\}, $ where $x$ and $y$ are measured in meters. Find the moment of inertia of the plate about the origin.
question.explanation:
For a plane lamina $D$ with mass density function $\lambda(x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

  • The moment of inertia about the $x$-axis is given by \[ I_x = \iint\limits_D y^2\lambda(x,y) \:\textrm{d}A. \]

  • The moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is given by \[ I_y = \iint\limits_D x^2\lambda(x,y) \:\textrm{d}A. \]

  • The moment of inertia about the origin is given by \[ I_0 = \iint\limits_D (x^2+y^2) \lambda(x,y) \:\textrm{d}A = I_x + I_y. \]

The area of the rectangular plate $D$ is $\mathcal{A} = 1\cdot2 = 2.$

Since the plate has uniform density, every unit of area contains the same amount of mass. Therefore, the mass density is constant and is given by the total mass divided by the total area:

\[ \lambda(x,y) = \dfrac{M}{\mathcal{A}} = \dfrac{M}{2}. \]

Using the formula for $I_0,$ we get

\begin{align*} I_0 &= \iint\limits_D (x^2+y^2) \lambda(x,y) \:\textrm{d}A \\ &= \dfrac{M}{2} \int_0^2 \int_0^1 x^2 + y^2 \:\textrm{d}x \:\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{M}{2} \int_0^2 \left[ \dfrac13x^3 + xy^2 \right]_{x=0}^{x=1} \:\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{M}{2} \int_0^2 \dfrac13 + y^2 \:\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{M}{2} \left[ \dfrac13y + \dfrac13y^3 \right]_0^2 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{M}{2} \left( \dfrac23 + \dfrac83 \right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{M}{2} \cdot \dfrac{10}3 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{5M}{3}. \end{align*}

Therefore, the moment of inertia is $\dfrac{5M}{3}\,\textrm{kg}\cdot \textrm{m}^2.$

example.title: Calculating the Moment of Inertia of a Lamina With Uniform Mass Density

question.text: A rectangular plate occupies the region $ D = \big\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 2, \:\: 0 \leq y \leq 3 \big\} $ with mass density function $\lambda(x,y) = (6-xy)\,\textrm{kg}/ \textrm{m}^2,$ where $x$ and $y$ area measured in meters. Find the moment of inertia of this lamina about the origin.
question.explanation:
For a plane lamina $D$ with mass density function $\lambda(x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

  • The moment of inertia about the $x$-axis is given by \[ I_x = \iint\limits_D y^2\lambda(x,y) \:\textrm{d}A. \]

  • The moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is given by \[ I_y = \iint\limits_D x^2\lambda(x,y) \:\textrm{d}A. \]

  • The moment of inertia about the origin is given by \[ I_0 = \iint\limits_D (x^2+y^2) \lambda(x,y) \:\textrm{d}A = I_x + I_y. \]

Using the formula for $I_0,$ we get

\begin{align*} I_0 &= \iint\limits_D (x^2+y^2) \lambda(x,y) \:\textrm{d}A \\ &= \int_0^3 \int_0^2 (x^2+y^2)(6-xy) \:\textrm{d}x \:\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \int_0^3 \left[ \int_0^2 6x^2 - x^3y + 6y^2 - xy^3 \:\textrm{d}x \right] \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \int_0^3 \left[ 2x^3 - \dfrac14x^4y + 6xy^2 - \dfrac12x^2y^3 \right]_{x=0}^{x=2} \:\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \int_0^3 16 - 4y + 12y^2 - 2y^3 \:\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \Big[ 16y - 2y^2 + 4y^3 - \dfrac12y^4 \Big]_0^3 \\[5pt] &= 48 - 18 + 108 - \dfrac{81}2 - 0 \\[5pt] &=97.5. \end{align*}

Therefore, the moment of inertia of the lamina about the origin is $97.5\,\textrm{kg}\cdot \textrm{m}^2.$

example.title: Calculating the Moment of Inertia of a Lamina Given a Mass Density Function

question.text: A rectangular plate occupies the region $ D = \big\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq3, \:\: 0 \leq y \leq 1 \big\} $ with mass density function $\lambda(x,y) = (4y +1)\,\textrm{kg}/ \textrm{m}^2,$ where $x$ and $y$ area measured in meters. Find the moment of inertia of this lamina about the origin.
question.explanation:
For a plane lamina $D$ with mass density function $\lambda(x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

  • The moment of inertia about the $x$-axis is given by \[ I_x = \iint\limits_D y^2\lambda(x,y) \:\textrm{d}A. \]

  • The moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is given by \[ I_y = \iint\limits_D x^2\lambda(x,y) \:\textrm{d}A. \]

  • The moment of inertia about the origin is given by \[ I_0 = \iint\limits_D (x^2+y^2) \lambda(x,y) \:\textrm{d}A = I_x + I_y. \]

Using the formula for $I_0,$ we get

\begin{align*} I_0 &= \iint\limits_D (x^2+y^2) \lambda(x,y) \:\textrm{d}A \\ &= \int_0^1 \int_0^3 (x^2+y^2)(4y+1) \:\textrm{d}x \:\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \int_0^1 \left[ \int_0^3 4x^2y +x^2 + 4y^3+ y^2 \:\textrm{d}x \right] \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \int_0^1 \left[ \dfrac{4}{3}x^3y + \dfrac{1}{3}x^3 + 4xy^3 + xy^2 \right]_{x=0}^{x=3} \:\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \int_1^2 36y+9+12y^3+3y^2 \:\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \Big[ 18y^2 + 9y + 3y^4 + y^3 \Big]_0^1 \\[5pt] &= 18 + 9 + 3 + 1 \\[5pt] &=31. \end{align*}

Therefore, the moment of inertia of the lamina about the origin is $31\,\textrm{kg}\cdot \textrm{m}^2.$

example.title: Calculating the Moment of Inertia of a Lamina Given a Mass Density Function

question.text: A rectangular plate occupies the region $ D = \big\{ (x,y) \: : \: 2 \leq x \leq 4, \:\: 0 \leq y \leq \ln{2} \big\} $ with mass density function $\lambda(x,y) = xe^{2y}\,\textrm{kg}/ \textrm{m}^2,$ where $x$ and $y$ area measured in meters. Find the moment of inertia of this lamina about the $y$-axis.
question.explanation:
For a plane lamina $D$ with mass density function $\lambda(x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

  • The moment of inertia about the $x$-axis is given by \[ I_x = \iint\limits_D y^2\lambda(x,y) \:\textrm{d}A. \]

  • The moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is given by \[ I_y = \iint\limits_D x^2\lambda(x,y) \:\textrm{d}A. \]

  • The moment of inertia about the origin is given by \[ I_0 = \iint\limits_D (x^2+y^2) \lambda(x,y) \:\textrm{d}A = I_x + I_y. \]

Using the formula for $I_y,$ we get

\begin{align*} I_y &= \iint\limits_D x^2 \lambda(x,y) \:\textrm{d}A \\ &= \int_0^{\ln{2}} \int_2^4 x^2\cdot xe^{2y} \:\textrm{d}x \:\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \int_0^{\ln{2}} \left[ \int_2^4 x^3e^{2y} \:\textrm{d}x \right] \textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \int_0^{\ln{2}} e^{2y} \left[ \dfrac{1}{4}x^4\right]_{2}^{4} \:\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \int_0^{\ln{2}} 60e^{2y} \:\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \Big[ 30e^{2y} \Big]_0^{\ln{2}} \\[5pt] &= 120 - 30 \\[5pt] &=90. \end{align*}

Therefore, the moment of inertia of the lamina about the $y$-axis is $90\,\textrm{kg}\cdot \textrm{m}^2.$

example.title: Calculating the Moment of Inertia of a Lamina Given a Mass Density Function

question.text: A rectangular plate of mass $M\,\textrm{kg}$ and uniform mass density occupies the region $ D = \big\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 3, \:\: 1 \leq y \leq 4 \big\}, $ where $x$ and $y$ are measured in meters. Find the moment of inertia of the plate about the origin.
question.explanation:
For a plane lamina $D$ with mass density function $\lambda(x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

  • The moment of inertia about the $x$-axis is given by \[ I_x = \iint\limits_D y^2\lambda(x,y) \:\textrm{d}A. \]

  • The moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is given by \[ I_y = \iint\limits_D x^2\lambda(x,y) \:\textrm{d}A. \]

  • The moment of inertia about the origin is given by \[ I_0 = \iint\limits_D (x^2+y^2) \lambda(x,y) \:\textrm{d}A = I_x + I_y. \]

The area of the rectangular plate $D$ is $\mathcal{A} = 3\cdot 3 = 9.$

Since the plate has uniform density, every unit of area contains the same amount of mass. Therefore, the mass density is constant and is given by the total mass divided by the total area: \[ \lambda(x,y) = \dfrac{M}{\mathcal{A}} = \dfrac{M}{9}. \]

Using the formula for $I_0,$ we get

\begin{align*} I_0 &= \iint\limits_D (x^2+y^2) \lambda(x,y) \:\textrm{d}A \\ &= \dfrac{M}{9} \int_1^4 \int_0^3 x^2 + y^2 \:\textrm{d}x \:\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{M}{9} \int_1^4 \left[ \dfrac13x^3 + xy^2 \right]_{x=0}^{x=3} \:\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{M}{9} \int_1^4 9 + 3y^2 \:\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{M}{9} \left[ 9y + y^3 \right]_1^4 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{M}{9} \left( 36+64 -9-1 \right) \\[5pt] &=10M \end{align*}

Therefore, the moment of inertia is $10M\,\textrm{kg}\cdot \textrm{m}^2.$
